headline: High-risk shared filesystem and git overlap: Gemini CLI can inject, leak, and cascade errors into semantica by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files, use MCP, and shares state with other instances via filesystem and git; semantica also reads/writes files and uses MCP. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if semantica consumes Gemini-authored files or MCP outputs as trusted content. The pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Gemini-written files or MCP resources as instructions
IF both agents operate in the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic parsing of agent-generated files
Require provenance tags on MCP/file inputs
Review shared git diffs before consumption
requires-engineering: add trust boundaries between agent outputs and instruction channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read local files and write files, and Gemini CLI explicitly touches files in cwd plus shell environment while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, secrets, and audit trails. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive material through outputs or synced files. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, and the blast radius includes secrets and regulated data.
conditions: IF the agents share a filesystem or git working tree
IF sensitive enterprise data is present in files readable by either agent
mitigations: Use separate OS users
Mount distinct workspaces read-only where possible
Remove secrets from shared directories
Restrict network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. Gemini CLI shares state via filesystem and git; semantica uses a shared intelligence layer across instances. Concurrent writes to the same repo or mutable resources can corrupt state or overwrite each other without locking. This is a default-dangerous overlap with clear conflict potential.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or mutable directory
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Serialize write access
Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent during git operations
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce shell and file outputs that semantica may ingest into its shared context graph, provenance, or decision records. If semantica treats those outputs as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into persistent graph state or downstream actions. Both profiles document the necessary input/output surfaces, so the risk is credible and not merely speculative.
conditions: IF semantica imports Gemini CLI outputs into its graph without verification
IF downstream workflows act on semantica decision records or provenance
mitigations: Require human review before ingestion
Validate outputs against source files
Mark Gemini outputs as untrusted provenance
Limit semantica writes to staging graphs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before persistence

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI is Google-hosted and handles API keys and shell environment, while semantica is self-hosted but handles enterprise data, contracts, and audit trails. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through Gemini's cloud-backed API path, compliance obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated enterprise data is sent through Gemini CLI's external API path
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not matched by Google-hosted processing
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Gemini prompts
Use redacted samples only
Confirm DPA and residency terms
Route sensitive work to semantica only
requires-engineering: document retention and deletion controls
